nodes.label: 01-relational-model
nodes.description: Tables, keys, constraints, normalization (1NF-BCNF), denormalization, surrogate vs natural keys, Postgres data types, JSONB/arrays, foreign-key scale strategy

nodes.label: Codd relational model (1970)
nodes.description: Relations as sets of tuples, typed domains, closed algebra (selection, projection, join, union)

nodes.label: Primary key constraint
nodes.description: Non-null unique identifier per row, one per table, enforced by engine

nodes.label: Foreign key constraint
nodes.description: Multi-column reference to PK/unique key on another table, with ON DELETE/UPDATE clauses (NO ACTION, RESTRICT, CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT)

nodes.label: Normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF
nodes.description: Progressive elimination of redundancy: 1NF (atomic cells), 2NF (whole PK), 3NF (PK only), BCNF (determinant=candidate key)

nodes.label: Surrogate vs natural keys
nodes.description: Surrogate (DB-generated, opaque): stable under business-key changes; Natural (business data): changeable, cascades on PK changes. Production default: surrogate PK + unique natural key

nodes.label: JSONB for unbounded schema
nodes.description: JSONB (binary, GIN-indexable) for schema-varying or unstructured data; wrong use: replacing a join table

nodes.label: 02-indexes
nodes.description: B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN index types; partial indexes; covering indexes; leading-column rule; HOT updates; fillfactor

nodes.label: B-tree index structure
nodes.description: Balanced tree for range/equality queries, row-locator TIDs, leaf-page doubling on growth, tuning via fillfactor

nodes.label: GIN (Generalized Inverted Index)
nodes.description: Inverted index for multi-key data (arrays, JSONB, full text); slower write, faster search when selectivity is low

nodes.label: GiST (Generalized Search Tree)
nodes.description: Spatial indexes for geometric/range types; slower than B-tree on traditional range but supports custom ops (PostGIS)

nodes.label: BRIN (Block Range INdex)
nodes.description: Lightweight range index for large sequentially-inserted tables; tiny size, good selectivity on range predicates

nodes.label: Partial index
nodes.description: Index on WHERE clause subset (e.g., active=true); smaller, faster maintenance, enables index-only scans on filtered queries

nodes.label: Covering index
nodes.description: Index with INCLUDE columns for index-only scans; avoids heap fetch for non-indexed but included columns

nodes.label: HOT (Heap-Only Tuples)
nodes.description: Update that does not change indexed columns stays on same heap page, avoids index re-insert

nodes.label: 03-execution-plans
nodes.description: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE, scan types, join algorithms, pg_statistic, ANALYZE tuning, row-estimate errors, non-sargable predicates

nodes.label: Postgres planner
nodes.description: Enumeration + cost model: reads SQL, consults pg_statistic for selectivity, estimates rows per node, chooses cheapest plan tree

nodes.label: Seq Scan (sequential scan)
nodes.description: Full heap scan; cost = relpages×seq_page_cost + reltuples×cpu_tuple_cost; optimal for large predicates or no index

nodes.label: Index Scan
nodes.description: Walk index tree to find TIDs, fetch heap rows; cost grows with random_page_cost×matching_rows; optimal for few rows

nodes.label: Bitmap Heap Scan
nodes.description: Bitmap from one+ indexes sorted by physical location, then heap scan in order; turns random I/O sequential; optimal for medium-to-large selectivity

nodes.label: Index Only Scan
nodes.description: No heap fetch when index contains all needed columns and visibility map shows all-visible pages; fastest scan type

nodes.label: Nested Loop join
nodes.description: For each outer row, look up inner via index; cost = outer_rows×inner_cost; wins when outer small, inner indexed

nodes.label: Hash Join
nodes.description: Build hash table from smaller side, probe with larger; cost = build+probe; wins for medium-large equi-joins without index

nodes.label: Merge Join
nodes.description: Sort both sides (or use index order), merge in parallel; wins when both sides already sorted or spills efficient

nodes.label: pg_statistic catalog
nodes.description: Per-column statistics from ANALYZE: n_distinct, most_common_vals/freqs (MCV list), histogram_bounds, correlation

nodes.label: Row estimate error cascade
nodes.description: Misestimate on one node cascades into wrong join choice; planner picks Nested Loop expecting 10 outer, gets 10k; 1000× slowdown

nodes.label: Sargable predicate
nodes.description: Predicate usable by index (WHERE col >= value); non-sargable: function on indexed column (WHERE LOWER(col)=x), type coercion, leading wildcard

nodes.label: 04-mvcc-isolation
nodes.description: MVCC snapshots, transaction isolation levels (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable), bloat, autovacuum, HOT chains, SSI

nodes.label: MVCC snapshot
nodes.description: Per-transaction view of committed rows at transaction start; each row tagged with xmin/xmax; reader sees only rows visible in its snapshot

nodes.label: Read Committed isolation
nodes.description: Snapshot taken per statement; allows phantom reads, non-repeatable reads; most common in OLTP

nodes.label: Repeatable Read isolation
nodes.description: Snapshot held per transaction; prevents non-repeatable reads; allows phantoms (new rows matching WHERE)

nodes.label: Serializable isolation (SSI)
nodes.description: Prevents all anomalies including phantoms via Serialization-Snapshot-Isolation; detects conflicts, aborts on conflict

nodes.label: Bloat (dead tuples)
nodes.description: UPDATE/DELETE leave xmax-tagged tuples on disk; wasted space, slower scans; VACUUM reclaims and marks for reuse

nodes.label: Autovacuum daemon
nodes.description: Background process triggers VACUUM/ANALYZE on tables exceeding thresholds (default 50 + 10% of reltuples); tunable per table

nodes.label: HOT chain (HOT-visible)
nodes.description: Chain of xmax-linked tuples from HOT update; VACUUM collapses chains to recover space

nodes.label: 05-pooling
nodes.description: PgBouncer modes (session/transaction/statement), client/server pools, pool sizing, prepared statements in transaction mode, Supavisor/Odyssey/PgCat

nodes.label: Connection pool
nodes.description: Cache of reusable pre-opened TCP connections; client-side (5-20 per worker) + server-side (PgBouncer, 20-100 backends)

nodes.label: PgBouncer session mode
nodes.description: 1:1 backend per client connection; no multiplexing; SET, LISTEN, session-level advisory locks all work

nodes.label: PgBouncer transaction mode
nodes.description: Backend leased per transaction; real multiplexing (10k clients on 50 backends); breaks SET (use SET LOCAL), LISTEN, SQL PREPARE (use protocol PREPARE)

nodes.label: Postgres backend cost
nodes.description: Per connection: ~5-10 MB RSS, proc-table slot, context-switch overhead; throughput peaks ~(cores×2)+spindles, degrades linearly past

nodes.label: Pool sizing formula
nodes.description: Connections = worker_count × (concurrent_requests × db_calls_per_request × avg_query_ms / request_budget_ms); or HikariCP: (cores×2)+spindles

nodes.label: Idle-in-transaction timeout
nodes.description: GUC: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (e.g., 60s); Postgres aborts backends idle in transaction past threshold

nodes.label: Prepared statements in transaction mode
nodes.description: PgBouncer 1.21+ supports protocol-level prepared statements (driver-managed); max_prepared_statements > 0 enables rewrite/re-prepare per backend

nodes.label: 06-migrations
nodes.description: DDL lock matrix, expand-contract, ADD COLUMN/NOT NULL/type-change safety, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, pgroll/Atlas/Squawk, lock_timeout discipline

nodes.label: Postgres lock matrix
nodes.description: Eight lock modes (ACCESS SHARE to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE); EXCLUSIVE conflicts with everything; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) safe for DML

nodes.label: Lock queue blocking
nodes.description: DDL waits for lock; new queries queue behind DDL even if they need weaker locks; one slow SELECT + ALTER TABLE = table frozen

nodes.label: Expand-contract pattern
nodes.description: Breaking change = additive expand step (before code deploy) + removal contract step (after code drain); each reversible

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN instant (PG 11+)
nodes.description: Constant DEFAULT instant (metadata only); volatile DEFAULT rewrites table; no DEFAULT instant but all NULLs

nodes.label: NOT NULL constraint safe pattern
nodes.description: ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID (enforce new, not old) + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (light lock, scans without blocking writes) + ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.description: Non-blocking index build; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock; 2-3× slower; can fail leaving INVALID index (detect, DROP, retry)

nodes.label: lock_timeout GUC
nodes.description: Per-session timeout for acquiring lock (e.g., 2s); migration aborts cleanly if lock unavailable; retry with backoff

nodes.label: 07-sharding
nodes.description: Shard keys, hash/range/list/directory strategies, co-location, hot-shard failure, Citus distributed tables, schema-based sharding, online resharding

nodes.label: Shard key
nodes.description: Column determining which physical Postgres instance holds a row; hash/range/lookup to shard number; must be selective, uniform, stable, available at routing

nodes.label: Hash sharding
nodes.description: shard = hash(key) mod N; uniform distribution; rebalancing hard (changing N moves most rows)

nodes.label: Range sharding
nodes.description: Shard owns key range; natural for time-series; rebalancing easier (split range); risk of hot tail (newest on one shard)

nodes.label: Directory-based sharding
nodes.description: External shard_map table: key → shard; most flexible; allows per-tenant moves; adds lookup cost

nodes.label: Hot shard failure mode
nodes.description: One shard receives disproportionate traffic (poor key choice or tenant growth); effective throughput = one-shard capacity

nodes.label: Co-location in sharded cluster
nodes.description: Tables with same shard key live on same workers; joins by shard key stay local; without: cross-shard fan-out, orders of magnitude slower

nodes.label: Citus distributed tables
nodes.description: Rows split by shard key across worker nodes; hash into N shards (default 32-128); coordinator plans, routes, aggregates

nodes.label: Citus reference tables
nodes.description: Full copy on every worker; for tables joined to many distributed tables; updates via 2PC across workers

nodes.label: Schema-based sharding (Citus 12+)
nodes.description: Each tenant gets a schema; Citus distributes schemas across workers; no shared key needed; per-schema isolation

nodes.label: Cross-shard queries
nodes.description: Queries without shard-key filter fan out to all shards; coordinator aggregates; cost N× work, P99 = max(shard latencies)

nodes.label: Distributed transactions (2PC)
nodes.description: Multi-shard transaction: prepare all shards; if all OK commit all; if any fail rollback all; latency and risk trade-off

nodes.description: Seven-tier scaling model from schema design through sharding; measuring bottlenecks; when to scale; integration of all previous pieces

nodes.label: Seven-tier scaling model
nodes.description: 1. Schema design + constraints, 2. Indexes + query optimization, 3. Connection pooling, 4. Read replicas, 5. Caching, 6. Vertical scaling, 7. Sharding

nodes.label: MVCC snapshot hold blocks vacuum
nodes.description: Long transaction holds snapshot; blocks VACUUM from reclaiming rows; causes bloat; interacts with autovacuum tuning

nodes.label: Planner uses index selectivity in cost model
nodes.description: Index selectivity from pg_statistic drives scan choice (Seq vs Index); stale statistics → wrong scan type → bad performance

nodes.label: Migrations acquire DDL locks blocking transactions
nodes.description: ALTER TABLE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; blocks DML; long migration blocks all subsequent queries; requires lock_timeout + retries

nodes.label: Idle-in-transaction blocks vacuum in pooled environments
nodes.description: Connection released to pool but transaction not closed; snapshot held; blocks VACUUM; hidden bug in migration code or error handling
